title: Check the links between projects

blocks.text: Each project row has passed its own checks. What is left are the rules no single row can break: they are about how rows refer to each other. In the selection model each project $`i`$ has one binary $`x_i`$, a child $`c`$ has the row $`x_c \le x_{p(c)}`$ (parent), and an alternative group $`g`$ has the row $`\sum_{i \in g} x_i \le 1`$ (alt).

Write `link_problems(projects)` in `links.py`. `projects` is a list of `Project` records (defined at the top of the file): `pid`, `parent` (an id, or `None`) and `group` (an alternative group, or `None`). It returns one string per problem, in any order:

rows: `<id>` appears in more than one record (once per id, however many copies)
project `<id>` names itself as its parent
project `<id>` names a parent that no record has, anywhere in the list
child `<id>` is in the same alternative group as its parent

blocks.text: Why is the last one a problem? If child $`c`$ and its parent $`p`$ share a group, the model has both $`x_c + x_p \le 1`$ (alt) and $`x_c \le x_p`$ (parent). Funding $`c`$ ($`x_c = 1`$) would need $`x_p = 1`$ by the parent row, and then the alt row reads $`1 + 1 \le 1`$, which is false. So $`x_c = 0`$ in every allowed plan: the child can never be funded, and the data is surely wrong.
A project with no group shares a group with nobody. A self-parent is reported only as `self-parent`.

works = [

    Project("H2", parent="H1", group="pump"),
    Project("H3", parent="H3"),
    Project("H4", parent="H9"),
    Project("H5", group="pump"),
    Project("H5"),
]
print("problems:", link_problems(works))
print("problems for H1 and child H6:", link_problems(works[:1] + [Project("H6", parent="H1")]))

cases.says: a list whose ids, parents and groups are consistent has no problems
a child whose parent is in no row is reported
a child in the same alternative group as its parent is reported
a parent listed after its child counts as known
an id that appears three times is one problem
a child and parent that both have no group are fine
a project that names itself as parent is reported as that, and only that

origin.section: A Rule Across Fields Goes in a Model Validator; a Rule Across Rows Goes Over the Whole File

concepts: uniqueness and references between rows are checked over the whole list, after each row is valid on its own
